newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks bottom out on industrial production.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks bottom out on industrial production.

text.p: Mexican stocks managed to recover very slightly from sharply weak levels after strong industrial output figures offered the market some respite at mid-morning, dealers said.
"The (industrial output) figures just have to have a big effect," a desk trader said. "The bourse is trying to recover, now, but before it was dropping like a stone."

The leading IPC share index was down 65.33 points, or 1.37 percent, at 4,711, but had reached as low as 4,678.14 on profit-taking exacerbated by fallout from even sharper falls on the Brazilian equity markets.
The Finance Ministry announced mid-morning that Mexico's industrial activity increased by 9.0 percent in May, compared to the same month last year.
Dealers said the relative recovery was most noticeable in shares listed by financial group Bancomer and Telfonos de Mxico (Telmex).

Bancomer B shares were down 8 centavos to 4.07 pesos, but had traded as low as 3.92 pesos, while the A shares had recovered from a low of 2.34 pesos to trade at 2.43 pesos, or down 6 centavos from Monday's close.
"The market had hit the (Bancomer) A shares particularly hard," a desk tarder said.
Telmex had meanwhile rebounded from a low of 20.30 pesos to trade at 20.55 pesos, down 25 centavos on the day.
Dealers said selling was still evident, however, addding that forecast gains in domestic interest rates at today's Cetes Treasury bill auction could thwart a full recovery in stocks.
